title: Austin Property Taxes, Bus Fares, and Urban Growth
summary:
*   **Property Tax Uproar:** Residents and businesses launched strong protests against recent property re-evaluations, which led to 200-900% tax increases in some areas. They urged a city-wide reassessment and suggested exploring alternative revenue sources like sales or room taxes.
*   **Public Transit Debates:** The city advanced a five-year bus service franchise, scheduling a public hearing for the ordinance. A major point of contention was the proposed school bus fare, sparking heated discussions over affordability and the operator's costs.
*   **Extensive Urban Development:** City leaders approved a large urban renewal project and numerous other zoning changes, frequently shifting land use towards commercial or higher-density residential. This signals significant ongoing development activity across Austin.
*   **Infrastructure & Fiscal Vigilance:** While awarding contracts for essential services like street lighting and power plant fuel, the city notably rejected bids for new transformers worth half a million dollars due to identical pricing, opting to re-bid annually to ensure competitive offers.

TO DISCUSS TAX EVALUATIONS
MR. ROGAN GILES represented the Austin Property Owners Association, comprised mostly of
large property owners and business operators in the northeast tax quadrant of the City,
including: Delwood Center; Sears Hancock Center; Capital Plaza: Cameron Village; Reagan
Square; Henna Chevrolet; Austin Truck and Machinery; Volkswagon; Lone Star Beer Central

Mr. Giles presented their case, stating this northeast quadrant had been re-evaluated, and
the results were a minimum of 200% increase up to 900% at least. The 1970-71 figures are

with the City Manager in an investigation as to what had been done in this quadrant and to

entire City be evaluated this way before these new values are applied with the tax rate.

clients, as some had competition in areas in the City that had not been re-evaluated; and

opposition to the one quadrant's being re-evaluated at the high increase, while other

AUSTIN TAXPAYERS LEAGUE TAXES
At 11:00 A.M., the Council heard representatives from the Austin Taxpayers Three League.
Mr. George Shepherd and the Executive Committee appeared.
Resolutions adopted by the League were read pointing out: (1) The 26th Street North and
Shoal Creek East area had been assessed at a 100% 400% increase, placing hardships on
retired property owners or those limited salaries; and requesting the Council to rescind
the 1970 tax plan, "re-evaluations", until all areas of Austin had likewise been
reappraised in order to more fairly distribute the tax burden to all citizens; and that
the Council study other methods of maintaining current property value records; (2) That
the Council study other sources of income to supplement increased property taxes which
harm the fixed wage earner and retired home owner; (3) That the Council thoroughly explain
to the taxpayers the need for increased taxes so the citizens might understand the cause
for recent drastic property valuation increases; and that the Council establish as a
policy not to enter into projects that will materially increase the present tax structure
without allowing public notifications and reasonable time for citizens to be heard. The
Mr. Shepherd also asked for break-down figures in the quadrants.
Mayor reported that the City Manager had been asked to get the information for which Mr.
Shepherd had asked.
